note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Open seat (Gov. Polis term-limited). Marx's repro stance is from third-party reporting, absent from his platform; labeled accordingly.

CO-governor.statusNote: Open seat: AG Phil Weiser (D), who beat Sen. Michael Bennet in the primary, faces ministry founder Victor Marx (R), who won by 2,515 votes in what appears to be the closest Republican governor primary in state history.

candidates.name: Phil Weiser
candidates.background: Colorado Attorney General since 2019; former CU Law dean and clerk to Justices White and Ginsburg. Son and grandson of Holocaust survivors. Has filed 64 lawsuits against the Trump administration since January 2025. Beat Sen. Michael Bennet about 55-45 in the June primary.
priorities: Cost of living and housing affordability
Defending Coloradans' rights against federal overreach

cost.label: Pairs business-friendly regulatory review ('regulations should be treated like garlic') with state investment in childcare and health care (Colorado Sun issue guide)

health.label: 'Healthy Colorado Plan': universal primary care, building on the Colorado Option, insulin caps, surprise-billing ban (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed: 40,000 attainable homes via faster permitting and lower fees AND down-payment help plus a ban on algorithmic rent collusion by corporate landlords (campaign site)

immigration.label: Enforce state laws barring federal coercion of local police into immigration enforcement and blocking ICE detention facility sales (campaign site)

taxes.label: Mixed: keep TABOR's voter-approval requirement for tax increases; open to revenue changes for childcare (Colorado Sun issue guide)

climate.label: Meet emission-reduction goals: Geothermal Development Authority, battery storage, EV incentives, heat-pump rates (campaign site)

education.label: Livable teacher wages plus teacher housing aid; defend public schools against privatization; expand Universal Preschool (campaign site)

safety.label: Mixed: police recruitment and modernized training AND co-responder mental-health teams, risk-based bail (campaign site)

repro.label: Defend reproductive rights 'including Amendment 79 and against any attacks on our laws protecting the right to choose' (campaign site)

democracy.label: 'Defend Colorado's gold-standard voting laws against political power plays and retaliation' (campaign site)

candidates.name: Victor Marx
candidates.background: Founder of a religious humanitarian nonprofit and Marine Corps veteran; a political newcomer who describes himself as a 'high-risk humanitarian.' Won the closest Republican gubernatorial primary in Colorado history, 39.9% to Barbara Kirkmeyer's 39.4%. Both his primary rivals have declined to support him.

cost.label: Mixed-market: expand earned-income tax credits and preserve the senior homestead exemption while deregulating home building; audit every executive agency (campaign policies)

health.label: Keep Cover All Coloradans for pregnant women and children already enrolled while auditing Medicaid for waste and fraud (Colorado Sun issue guide)

housing.label: Expedited permitting with statutory decision deadlines for home building; identify and roll back building, environmental, and energy mandates that raise construction costs (campaign policies)

immigration.label: End sanctuary policies, require cooperation with federal authorities, Border-Related Crime Strike Force (campaign policies)

taxes.label: Phased income-tax rate reduction when verified surpluses exist, veto new fees that act as de facto taxes, enforce TABOR limits (campaign policies)

climate.label: 'All-of-the-above' energy strategy expanding renewables 'while maintaining the vital role of oil, gas, hydroelectric power' (campaign policies)

education.label: Expand school choice via education savings accounts; parental curriculum access; local board control (campaign policies)

safety.label: Repeal 'soft-on-crime laws': end 'catch-and-release,' detain dangerous defendants, statewide fentanyl priority (campaign policies)

repro.label: Personally 'pro-life' but says he would not try to overturn Colorado's voter-approved abortion protections; absent from his own platform (Colorado Times Recorder)

democracy.label: Voter ID for all ballots, annual voter-roll maintenance, ballot chain-of-custody standards (campaign policies)

controversies.label: Ministry stories are largely unverifiable, including saying his stepfather forced him to kill a man at age 7; sidestepped debates and forums; rivals Kirkmeyer ('a disaster for our state') and Bottoms ('con man') said they would not support him (Colorado Sun)
Campaign website claim that his ministry rescued more than 40,000 women and children was disproven and removed; he has since declined to give an exact number (Wikipedia)
